intended_object: The real inner-product space ℓ²(\binom{[n]}{k}) ≅ ℝ^{\binom{n}{k}}. Its vectors are real functions on the k-th layer of the Boolean cube, that is, on the k-element subsets of {0,…,n−1}, and it carries the standard Euclidean inner product. I inferred this from the docstring, the name and the definition of `Level` in the same file.
explanation:
`Level n k` is defined as `{S : Finset (Fin n) // S.card = k}`, which is the set of k-subsets of [n] (the k-th layer of the Boolean cube). It has `Fintype.card = n.choose k`. `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Level n k)` is Mathlib's L² inner-product space of real functions on this finite index set. This is exactly the Euclidean space of layer functions that is standard in the linear-algebra / Johnson-scheme arguments for binary codes. The library already uses the bare function type `LayerFunction n k := Level n k → ℝ` with an explicit inner product `∑ S, f S * g S`; this abbrev attaches Mathlib's standard inner-product-space structure to the same carrier.

The object is specific: one particular finite index set. So it is not too narrow merely for being specific, and it reuses Mathlib's general `EuclideanSpace` construction instead of rebuilding it. Mathlib has no more specific named counterpart, so `mathlib_counterpart` is left empty. Degenerate cases also behave correctly: when k > n the layer is empty, and the space is the zero space, as it should be.
